extracted.intended_audience: general public; prospective researchers, students, funders, partners and collaborators
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional 'About us' profile describing the Francis Crick Institute's mission, strategy, structure, science programme, governance, funding and public engagement. Useful for readers assessing the institute's aims, scope and organizational model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — 'Discovery without boundaries'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Crick’s mission is discovery without boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We don’t limit the direction our research takes. The institute aims to understand how living things work to help improve treatment, diagnosis and prevention of human disease, and to generate economic opportunities for the UK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary scale and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 2,000 staff and students use their wide-ranging knowledge and expertise to work across disciplines and explore biology at all levels, from molecules through cells to entire organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on large, multidisciplinary teams and breadth of biological scales investigated; signals expectation of cross-disciplinary collaboration and depth across molecular to organismal biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy — 'Discovery Without Boundaries' (refreshed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our refreshed Discovery Without Boundaries strategy sets out how we carry out world-class discovery research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strategy frames institutional priorities and approaches for achieving high-impact discovery science across the institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science programme — broad and inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Our science programme is broad and inclusive, exploring biological mechanisms at all scales from molecules through cells to organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme values inclusivity of topics and approaches across the life sciences rather than narrow, prescriptive thematic limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to science — highest quality and at the forefront
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re conducting research of the highest quality right at the forefront of biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States an institutional standard of excellence and leadership in cutting-edge biomedical science; implies expectations for methodological rigor and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to understand more about how living things work to help improve treatment, diagnosis and prevention of human disease, and generate economic opportunities for the UK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions translational outcomes (clinical benefit, prevention, economic impact) as explicit aims alongside discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding partnerships and collaborative governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Crick is the outcome of a merger between the MRC's NIMR and CRUK's LRI and was established by six founding partner organisations: MRC, CRUK, Wellcome, UCL, Imperial College London and King’s College London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights multi-institutional founding structure as core to identity and operations; implies expectations for academic partnerships and secondments from partner universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — Board of Trustees
rubrics_metrics.description: The institute is governed by a Board of Trustees, comprised of independent members and representatives from each of our founding partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies governance model and stakeholder representation as part of institutional accountability and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding model — core funding plus external grants
rubrics_metrics.description: We are funded through core funding from the MRC, CRUK and Wellcome, as well as external research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes mixed funding streams (institutional/core funders plus project-based grants) that sustain institute operations and research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational growth and research group structure
rubrics_metrics.description: We began operating in our new, purpose-built institute in early 2017 and now have more than 100 research groups. Research groups from NIMR and LRI have been joined by groups seconded from each of our three partner universities, and we have recruited a significant number of newly recruited group leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys expectations about scale (number of groups), mechanisms for acquiring talent (secondments, recruitment), and the hybrid composition of groups (legacy + new hires).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement, access and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support us (Donate to help the Crick continue its discoveries). Visit us (The Crick is easily accessible by train, tube and bus). Contact us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates institutional commitments to public engagement, accessibility for visitors, and mechanisms for public support and contact.
